title: Why acceleration follows the net force
canonical_question: Why does the acceleration always point in the same direction as the net force?
summary: F = ma relates two vectors with mass, a positive number, between them.
Whatever way the leftover push points, the change in motion builds up that same way.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: The law is a vector equation
sections.body_md: F = ma relates two vectors with mass, a positive number, between them. Multiplying a vector by a positive number cannot change its direction, only its length. So acceleration must point exactly where the net force points.

sections.heading: What that means physically
sections.body_md: Whatever way the leftover push points, the change in motion builds up that same way. Push forward and the body speeds up forward; push sideways and its path bends toward the push. Direction of cause equals direction of effect.

key_points: F = ma is a vector equation.
Acceleration lines up with net force.
core.bridge_to_parent: It deepens why direction is shared, not how to compute it.
